title: Radiation and Ideal Radiator
notes: **Radiation:** heat transfer by electromagnetic waves, mainly infrared. It does not need a material medium and can travel through vacuum.
**Speed:** radiant heat travels at the speed of light, $c = 3 \times 10^8\,\text{m/s}$.
**Ideal radiator (black body):** a perfect emitter and absorber of radiation. It absorbs all incident radiation and emits the maximum possible radiation at every wavelength for its temperature.

**Wien's displacement law:** $\lambda_{max} T = b$, where $b \approx 2.898 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{m}\cdot\text{K}$. Hotter objects peak at shorter wavelengths: the Sun peaks in visible light, a hot iron glows red, a warm body peaks in infrared.
**Practical absorbers/emitters:** lamp-black and black paint are good approximations to ideal radiators; shiny polished surfaces are poor absorbers and poor emitters.
